instruction: Center the text horizontally on the canvas so it appears in the middle.

metadata.explanation: Task requires centering the text layer horizontally. Evaluator checks if the horizontal center of the text bounding box is within the middle 10% of the image width (5% tolerance on each side). Verified: GIMP provides alignment tools for centering layers.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies horizontal centering by analyzing the exported image to find text boundaries and comparing the text center against the image center
Postconfig appropriately exports the GIMP image to PNG format (Shift+Ctrl+E) for verification since GIMP layer state cannot be directly inspected after execution
Metric logic is sound: finds leftmost and rightmost dark pixels, calculates text center as (left_most + right_most) / 2, and checks if within middle 10% of image width
Complete coverage: instruction requires 'center text horizontally' and evaluator checks exactly that requirement
Expected parameter handling is correct: receives empty rules dict and doesn't use it (no incorrect access patterns)
Edge case handling: checks for None src_path and handles it gracefully
Minor concern: metric assumes text is darker than background (pixel < 128), which is reasonable given the orange_background.xcf file but could fail with inverted contrast
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a check to verify that text was actually found (e.g., if left_most == width or right_most == 0, return 0.0 with a warning)
Could make the algorithm more robust by supporting both dark-on-light and light-on-dark text scenarios
